question: Which of the 12,702 permute/transpose calls exist only to satisfy a downstream layout requirement and can be DELETED rather than accelerated.
instrument: perf/c14_layout/site_census.py -- a live-fold wrapper on ttnn.permute/transpose/reshape/to_layout that records the permutation ORDER, the tt_bio call stack and the producer of each input. A ttnn graph capture cannot answer this: it records operand shapes but arguments: [] , so the permutation order is unrecorded and a shape-preserving permute reads as the identity.

instrument_control.settled_case: two consecutive folds in one process must produce IDENTICAL per-site counts
instrument_control.settled_result: PASS -- 34,295 calls / 60 keys, fold0 == fold1 exactly
instrument_control.known_answer_case: the class total must reproduce c14-unpriced-block in-situ 71.4 GB / 11,672 calls for Transpose+Permute, an independent instrument on different data
instrument_control.known_answer_result: 75.5 GB / 12,702 calls = agreement to 5.7 % on bytes and 8.8 % on calls at a flat 2 B/element assumption

candidate.why_it_exists: ttnn.linear contracts the LAST dim, so the (C*D)=1024 axis has to be moved there. Nothing downstream needs the (rows, J, C*D) LAYOUT; it needs the CONTRACTION.
candidate.deletion: ttnn.matmul(z, o_weight, transpose_a=True) contracts dim -2 directly, so the permute goes away entirely rather than getting faster.
candidate.bytes_basis: 16 calls x 2 x 537.0 MB (read + write, both DRAM), from this row own live-fold census
candidate.rate_measured_where: c14-unpriced-block, the Transpose+Permute class OWN in-fold rate, in situ, c12-profiled-fold/runs/composed.json
candidate.crosscheck_basis: 22.7 % byte share of the parent 0.5997 s class total
candidate.op_level_prediction: arm B median <= 0.70 x arm A median
what_would_make_it_NEGATIVE: transpose_a=True is implemented on device as an explicit transpose inside the matmul -- the bytes move rather than go away, arm B >= arm A, lever dead at op level with no fold
transpose_a forces a matmul program config that loses the core_grid or the in0 reuse the shipped ttnn.linear gets, so the projection itself gets slower by more than the permute cost
arm B is not the same contraction -- caught by the float64 host reference, not by comparing two device arms
the fold does not reach this site at 512 aa on current main -- refuted: the census counted 16 live calls
candidate.standing_rule_acknowledged: An op-level number does NOT transfer to a fold. Four such numbers in C14 transferred at 25x-to-infinite error and two flipped sign. A win in this arm licenses BUILDING the lever and nothing else; only an interleaved benchlocked fold A/B with its own A/A floor on qb2 enters the ladder.

tenstorrent.py:3672 via 7271 and 7645.why: TriangleAttention(ending) transposes the whole 67.1 MB pair tensor in at 7271 and transposes the result back out at 7645 -- a genuine a->b->a pair, but with the entire attention between them. The transpose swaps the i and j axes, which is a BATCH-axis swap on [I,J,C]; no matmul flag absorbs that (transpose_a/transpose_b swap the last two dims, not dim 0 with dim 1). The projection LN(z)@W does commute with the swap, so the alternative is to transpose q,k,v,g instead of z -- strictly more bytes.
